title: osf bumps agnix-core 0.54.0 → 0.56.1
summary: A dependency-only change: the `osf` crate pins `agnix-core` from `=0.54.0` to `=0.56.1`, which drags its transitive `agnix-rules` crate from 0.54.0 to 0.56.5 in the lockfile. No source in this repository changes; what changes is the version of the lint/rule engine that `osf` links against at build time, and therefore the rule set and diagnostics that any osf command producing agnix output will emit.

lanes.subtitle: cargo workspace
lanes.summary: The repository's own crates. Only the osf manifest changes here; no source is touched.

nodes.label: osf

nodes.label: osf Cargo.toml
nodes.subtitle: agnix-core = "=0.56.1"
nodes.summary: The single authored line of this change: the exact-version pin on agnix-core is raised from 0.54.0 to 0.56.1. Because the pin is exact, nothing else in the workspace can pull a different agnix-core.

nodes.label: Cargo.lock
nodes.subtitle: resolved versions + checksums
nodes.summary: The lockfile records the new resolution: agnix-core 0.56.1 and its transitive agnix-rules 0.56.5, each with a new checksum. This is the artifact that makes the bump reproducible across machines and CI.

nodes.label: agnix-core
nodes.summary: The lint/rule engine osf depends on. Two minor versions forward: the API surface osf calls is expected to be compatible, but the rules and diagnostics it produces are not frozen.

nodes.label: agnix-rules
nodes.summary: Transitive dependency of agnix-core, pulled forward automatically by the bump. This is where the actual rule definitions live, so it is the crate most likely to change observable output.

edges.label: manifest
edges.summary: The crate is described by its manifest; the manifest is the only file in the crate that changed.
The change itself: an exact-version pin raised two minor versions. Exact pins mean this is the only place the version can be chosen.

edges.label: resolution
edges.summary: Cargo re-resolves the graph from the new constraint and rewrites the lockfile entries and checksums.

edges.label: transitive
edges.summary: agnix-core pulls agnix-rules forward with it; the rules crate moves further (0.56.5) than the core crate (0.56.1).

flows.title: How the new pin reaches the build
flows.summary: The ordered path from the edited constraint to the compiled artifact: the manifest pin is re-resolved, the lockfile is rewritten, and the two agnix crates are fetched at their new versions.

messages.label: resolve 0.56.1

messages.note: The transitive rules crate is pulled forward as a consequence, not by an explicit edit.

messages.label: lockfile entries + checksums
messages.note: The resolved graph is frozen back into Cargo.lock, which is what CI and other machines will build from.
